title: Heterogeneous GPU isolation: per-tenant bandwidth caps, soft-eviction, and headroom guarantees
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement:
Customers running Dedicated pools with mixed tenant workloads observe tail-latency impact from a small number of noisy tenants. Current soft quota and slab allocation approaches provide gross-level isolation but do not handle heterogeneous GPU mixes (A100 vs H100) or bursty KV/cache-heavy workloads well. We need a tenant-level isolation mechanism that: (1) enforces bandwidth/throughput caps per-tenant across heterogeneous hardware, (2) provides configurable headroom guarantees for SLO-backed tenants, and (3) supports soft-eviction/preemption signals rather than hard killing, to preserve QoE for interactive apps.

Goal:
Design and implement a GPU-level isolation layer plus scheduler hooks that rate-limit token-generation bandwidth per-tenant, surface soft-eviction signals (graceful degrade paths), and reserve headroom for guaranteed throughput contracts. The implementation should be compatible with Dedicated autoscaling policies, integrate with the runtime's KV cache eviction strategy, and expose metrics and alerts in Console for operations and SRE teams.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: scheduler plugin, per-tenant bandwidth accounting, eviction/preemption scoring, headroom reservation API, metrics + console dashboard, integration tests against mixed-HW simulation.
- Out-of-scope: multi-tenant network-level QoS (handled by infra networking), full re-architecture of slab allocator (we'll add hooks, not rewrite).

Design summary:
We will add a tenant isolation layer with three components: (A) Accounting & Cap Enforcement: token throughput and GPU memory bandwidth approximations computed per-tenant at runtime using lightweight sampling; configurable caps (soft/hard) expressed as tokens/sec or GPU-throughput-priority points. (B) Headroom Reservation: allow customers to purchase "headroom slots" (reserved micro-capacity) that the scheduler treats as burstable credits against caps with guaranteed refill rate. (C) Preemption & Soft Eviction: instead of immediate job kill, we introduce a preemption score that triggers one of: throttling (reduce batching/beam width), KV-cache cold-start hints (drop cached prefixes), or graceful-request fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. The scheduler plugin computes scores using recency, sustained overuse, and customer SLA tier.

Trade-offs considered:
- Accounting overhead vs precision: we favor low-overhead sampling to avoid adding tail latency; worst-case precision +/- 5-10% is acceptable.
- Soft eviction complexity vs UX: multi-stage degrade paths are more complex but expected to reduce P0 incidents compared to blunt worker preemption.
- Heterogeneous hardware: normalize caps using a device-performance index (benchmarks -> points) so we can compare A100/H100 fairly without needing exact FLOP accounting.

Telemetry and observability:
Expose per-tenant metrics: current_tokens/sec, cap_limit, preemption_score, headroom_credits, eviction_action_taken. Add Console dashboard tile with per-pool heatmap and alert rule templates for sustained >85% cap usage or repeated preemption events.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for accounting and scoring math.
- Integration tests in CI with mixed GPU simulator (A100/H100 behavioral profile) to validate headroom refills and soft-eviction ordering.
- Canary rollout in Dedicated test pool with two pilot customers (internal teams first) and canary telemetry to validate SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler plugin added that enforces per-tenant throughput caps (tokens/sec) for mixed GPU pools and respects soft/hard cap config fields.
Headroom reservation API implemented and backed by credits visible in Console; headroom refills at configured rate and is consumed on bursts.
Preemption scoring and 3-stage soft-eviction implemented (throttle, cache-drop hint, fallback model) and exercised by integration tests.
Metrics emitted for per-tenant usage, cap utilization, preemption_score, and headroom credits; Console dashboard updated and an alert template provided.
End-to-end canary shows no regression in median latency and <5% increase in P95 for non-noisy tenants; noisy-tenant guilty actions reduce cross-tenant P95 by >=20% in test pool.
notes: Normalization table for device-performance-index will be maintained in runtime/benchmarks/device_index.csv (see design doc link).
We will reuse existing quota config objects where possible and extend with 'headroom' and 'soft_cap' fields to avoid duplicating config surfaces.
Security flagged: preemption may expose tenant metadata in scheduler decisions. Work with security to ensure aggregated metrics do not leak tenant-specific payloads (security review required).
